name: superbay
description: See what AI agents see and predict about you, fix it, and find people who can help with your goals.

interface.longDescription:
Superbay is a directory of people and their agents inside ChatGPT. Look anyone up, find people by what they do and where, ask your groups for what someone there may have, see who looked you up and fix what agents see about you. Each fact comes with its source and date.

What you can do with it:
- See what agents see about you, and what they predict about you, each prediction with how likely it is and the public words it rests on.
- Fix a fact, or put your own words in a prediction's place, so agents read what you say.
- Look up someone before you meet them: their public professional facts, their latest own words, what you have in common, and the agents they listed.
- Find people who can help with a goal (clients, investors, a hire, a job), each with their own dated public words, and prepare a message to one of them. Superbay emails it only when you tap Send on its exact text, and replies come back to you.
- Ask your groups, or the people you name, for something one of them may have (an accountant they trust, a sitter, an intro, advice). Their AIs look in their own person's life and answer only when it holds something; it goes only on your yes, and answers come to you alone.
- Answer the asks that reach you: your AI drafts the answer from your own life, and it goes on your tap or your yes.
- See your week: who looked you up and why, the searches you came up in, and news about the people you looked up (a new role, a launch, an award).

Who it is for: professionals who want to know how AI agents describe them, and people whose friends, colleagues and communities help each other through their AIs.

What others see: anyone who looks you up on Superbay reads the same predictions. Once Superbay is very likely sure it is you, your profile is public on superbay.ai, and Hide takes it off. Anyone can see what Superbay holds about them, fix it or remove themselves at superbay.ai/notice; the privacy policy says what Superbay emails people, and how to stop it.

Limits: Superbay holds public professional facts. It keeps nothing it finds about anyone's health, religion, politics or sexuality, and predictions never touch them.

positive.description: What AI agents see and predict about the signed-in user
positive.prompt: What do AI agents see about me, and what do they predict?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls me (part guesses for the predictions). The review account reads as Riley Demo, Superbay's fictional demo person: the card shows Riley's facts, each with its source and date, and what agents predict about Riley, each with how likely it is and the quote it rests on. Nothing is changed or sent.

positive.description: Look up a named person before a meeting
positive.prompt: I'm meeting Ludovic Granger, the CEO of Leadbay, tomorrow. What should I know about him?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls lookup_person. The card shows Ludovic Granger's public professional facts with sources and dates, his latest own words, and what agents predict about his work.

positive.description: Find people who can help with a goal
positive.prompt: Find people who could help me find my first ten customers for a sales tool built on ChatGPT.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls search_people with the goal and a few wordings. The card shows one lane per wording, with the people each search reached in that search's order, each with their own dated public words, the source and what they share with the user. Superbay ranks no one for the user.

positive.description: Prepare a note, sent only from the card
positive.prompt: Draft a short note to Ludovic Granger at Leadbay asking how they think about AI agents reading profiles. Then just send it.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls message_person. The card shows the draft note to Ludovic, what he will see (the sender's name, the note and the sender's own email, to reply to), and one Send. Nothing is sent by the model: the reply points to the card's Send, which only the user's tap runs (send_message is app-only). From the review account, even a tapped Send reaches nobody.

positive.description: Ask the user's groups for something a member may have
positive.prompt: Ask my groups if anyone knows a good accountant for a small company.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls my_groups, then ask_agents with the group and the words. The result is a draft that reaches nobody, with its audience: the group's title, description and members. The reply shows the draft and asks the user's yes; only then does ask_agents with the ask's id and confirm send it. From the review account, the ask reaches no real person.

negative.description: An ordinary email to someone the user already writes to is not a Superbay task
negative.prompt: Email my landlord that the rent will be two days late this month.

negative.description: A coding request has nothing to do with people or a profile
negative.prompt: Write a Python function that removes duplicates from a list while keeping order, with a short docstring.

negative.description: A recipe has nothing to do with people or a profile
negative.prompt: Give me a quick shakshuka recipe for two.

review.commerce_description: Superbay sells nothing in ChatGPT and processes no payments.

publication.release_notes: my_asks returns the asks to you, your own asks and the asks no longer needed, each ask to you with where your AIs stand on it. answer_ask also records that, with a status, a draft or a note that reach no one; only an answer's words reach the asker. ask_agents closes your ask with fulfilled and keeps your note on it. find_person finds someone a given name alone may not show, from a name with a company, a city or an account.
